s: God encourages Joshua to be strong and courageous and to keep the law. Israel prepares to cross the Jordan.
Rahab hides the two spies in Jericho and is promised safety.
The priests carry the ark into the Jordan, the river stops flowing, and Israel crosses on dry ground.
Twelve stones from the river are set up as a memorial.
The men are circumcised at Gilgal and the Passover is kept. The manna stops. A commander of the Lord's army appears to Joshua.
Israel marches around Jericho for seven days, and its walls fall. Rahab's family is saved.
Achan steals from the plunder, and Israel is defeated at Ai until his sin is punished.
Israel takes Ai. Joshua reads the law at Mount Ebal.
The Gibeonites trick Israel into a treaty.
God fights for Israel against five kings, and the sun stands still. Joshua conquers the south.
Joshua defeats the northern kings at the waters of Merom.
A list of the kings Israel conquered.
Land still to be taken, and the territory of the eastern tribes.
The dividing of the land begins. Caleb receives Hebron.
The territory of Judah. Jerusalem is not taken.
The territory of Ephraim.
The territory of Manasseh.
The tabernacle is set up at Shiloh. Benjamin's territory.
The territories of the remaining tribes. Joshua receives his town.
The cities of refuge.
Towns are given to the Levites. Every promise God made has been fulfilled.
The eastern tribes go home and build an altar, nearly causing a war until they explain.
Joshua's farewell: hold fast to the Lord and do not mix with the nations.
At Shechem Joshua renews the covenant: as for me and my house, we will serve the Lord. Joshua dies.

3: As the ark goes into the river, the waters stop and Israel enters the promised land. The Jordan is where Jesus will later be baptized.
